========== #192: Deferred follow-ups from PR #191 review (markdownlint runner, commit convention, ADR template polish) ==========
LABELS: 
Deferred follow-ups from the automated review of #191. The two blocking findings from that review (the `cliff.toml`/`CHANGELOG.md` divergence and the ADR H1 rule) were fixed in that PR; everything below was explicitly deferred.

Source: https://github.com/ebridges/wakil/pull/191 — the `pr-reviewer` review comment dated 2026-08-07.

### 1. markdownlint has no runner

`.markdownlint.yaml` landed in #191 with nothing that reads it: no CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `ty`, `ruff`, `pytest` only), no `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, no `package.json`, no mention in `CLAUDE.md`'s Dev Workflow block. It also can't express ignores, so a bare `npx markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"` lints `.venv/` and `.claude-pr/`.

**Deferred by decision** — the config was landed intentionally ahead of the runner. When the runner is added:

- use `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml` so `globs`/`ignores` can be set (at minimum `.venv`, `.claude-pr`, `tests/fixtures`)
- document the invocation in `CLAUDE.md`'s Dev Workflow block
- expect ~100 errors in tracked files at the time of writing, including `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:166,191,333` (MD032, MD038 ×6, MD033 ×2) and `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:129` (MD012)

`CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` are already clean as of #191 (the only remaining ADR hits are `0001:18` MD040, `0001:32` MD032, and `0002:28,113` MD034).

### 2. Commit-convention violations already on this branch

`CLAUDE.md` specifies gitmoji-prefixed Conventional Commits. Three commits don't comply, with real changelog consequences since `cliff.toml` sets `filter_commits = true`:

- `326673c meta(lint): ...` and `9039549 meta(config): ...` — `meta` matches no parser in `cliff.toml`'s `commit_parsers`, so both are dropped from the changelog entirely
- `f28e754 docs(adr): responses to PR feedback.` — no emoji, so it renders as `- Docs(adr): responses to PR feedback.`

Decide whether to rewrite the branch history before merge or accept the changelog gaps.

### 3. `LICENSE.md`'s new `# License` heading may break the license badge

`README.md:5` uses `img.shields.io/github/license/ebridges/wakil`, which relies on GitHub's `licensee`-based detection. Adding `# License` to `LICENSE.md:1` for MD041 may push the MIT text below `licensee`'s confidence threshold. Unverified — `licensee` wasn't run.

Either ignore `LICENSE.md` in the lint config (preferred) or use `# MIT License`, a title `licensee` recognizes and strips. Confirm the badge and the repo sidebar still read MIT after merge.

### 4. `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` entry ordering

Commit `326673c` relocated the 29.5-minute-enrich entry (2026-08-02) from the end of the file to ~line 39, bundled into a commit labelled "markdown lint fixes." The move is byte-identical and fixes no lint error, but the file's own header calls it an **append-only** log, and the result isn't date-ordered either: 08-05, 08-05, 08-02, 07-23, 07-18, 07-17, 07-09, 07-17, … with 07-28 entries near the bottom.

Either revert the move or do an explicit ordering pass in its own commit and document the intended order in the file's intro.

### 5. `## About` nests every entry beneath it

`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:9` and `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:9`. Every entry is an `###`, so adding `## About` makes the whole log a subsection of "About." No default markdownlint rule requires the heading. Either drop it or add a `## Entries` heading before the first entry.

### 6. `## Implementation` is "strongly preferred" but lives inside an HTML comment

`docs/adr/0000-template.md`. The copy instructions say to delete every HTML comment, so an author following them literally deletes the strongly-preferred section along with its guidance.

Suggested: promote `## Implementation` to a live heading with its guidance in a comment beneath it, and change the two genuinely-optional blocks (`Alternatives considered`, `Supersession relative to ADR NNNN`) to say "uncomment this section if it applies, otherwise delete it."

### 7. Nits

- `docs/adr/0000-template.md` cites pinpoint line numbers (0018 line 86, 0015 line 332, 0008 line 33, 0012 line 296). All correct today, but unlike the ADRs they cite, the template persists indefinitely and these go stale on any edit to those files. Consider citing by section name plus quoted phrase.
- `docs/adr/0000-template.md:3` — `status: template` is an invented frontmatter value, which sits awkwardly next to commit `887c136`'s message ("drop invented status values"). Harmless in practice: nothing in `src/` or `tests/` parses ADR frontmatter. The in-file rationale is reasonable; the commit message and the file just disagree.
- `CLAUDE.md:33` — the `docs/adr/0000-template.md` bullet uses a hyphen where every sibling bullet in that block uses an em dash.
- `README.md` — "establishing how they're structured" wraps awkwardly and overstates the case; "new ADRs start from `docs/adr/0000-template.md`" reads better.



========== #190: enrich silently ignores explicit --context instructions to produce a required output page, and still reports success ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

A workspace has an established per-subject pattern: each source of a given kind produces three artifacts — a raw source note, an entity-page update, and a **separate typed page in a specific directory** (`<restricted-dir>/<subject-slug>-<kind>.md`, `type: assessment`). Eight prior sources of this kind all produced all three.

For the ninth, `enrich` was given unusually explicit instructions:

```
--context "... Follow the established pattern used for the other eight: raw
source under sources/, a <typed page> at <restricted-dir>/<subject>-<kind>.md
(type: assessment, ...), and a Timeline entry on <entity page>. See
<restricted-dir>/<other-subject>-<kind>.md for the exact shape."
```

Result:

```
Enriched source #N: 2 file(s) written, 7 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
  + <entity page>
  + <company page>
```

The third artifact was never proposed. No warning, no mention of the instruction, exit 0.

## Why this is worth fixing

The two pages it *did* write are good. The failure is invisible: `enrich` reports success, and the only way to notice the missing page is to know the pattern and check by hand. In a batch of sources that gap ships silently.

Note the contrast with the directory-validation path (#187), which *hard-fails* the whole run over a mechanically-correctable path error. Here a substantive, explicitly-requested output is dropped with no signal at all. The severity assignments are inverted.

## Possible angles

- If `--context` routing instructions are only advisory, say so in the docs — right now nothing suggests they can be silently dropped, and their presence in the prompt implies they're binding.
- Consider surfacing a summary of instructions the proposal did *not* act on, so the operator can see what was ignored.
- A stronger option: a way to *require* an output (e.g. `--require-page <path>` or `--require-type <type>`) that fails the run when unmet, for exactly this repeating-pattern case.
- Sibling-precedent awareness would help generally: eight existing files matching `<restricted-dir>/*-<kind>.md` is a strong structural signal that a ninth belongs there, independent of anything in `--context`.

## Workaround

Wrote the page by hand and committed it onto the ingest branch.


========== #189: No PDF ingest handler — ingest has transcript/text/article only, so PDFs need manual pdftotext and lose their real origin ==========
LABELS: enhancement
## Gap

`wakil ingest` offers `transcript`, `text`, and `article`. There is no handler for PDFs, which is a common capture format for papers, reports, and print/share exports of web articles.

## What the workaround costs

To ingest two PDFs I had to:

1. `pdftotext` each into a scratch file, and hand-clean extraction artifacts (ligature/small-caps splitting mangles running heads — an all-caps framework name came out as `S KILLW EAVER` throughout a 14-page paper, which would otherwise have been indexed and embedded in that broken form).
2. Hand-prepend a header block with title/author/date/URL, since none of that survives extraction.
3. `wakil ingest text <scratch-path>`.
4. Go back afterwards and hand-fix `origin:` in the committed clipping, because step 3 recorded the **scratch path** as the origin — a `/private/tmp/...` path that will not exist tomorrow.

Step 4 is the damaging one: without it the vault permanently records a dead temp path as the provenance of a source. It is easy to forget and there is no warning.

## Suggested behaviour

A `wakil ingest pdf <path>` that:

- extracts text with a layout-aware extractor and normalises the common artifacts (ligatures, hyphenated line breaks, split small-caps runs)
- pulls embedded PDF metadata (Title, Author, CreationDate) and any DOI/arXiv ID found in the text, using them to seed frontmatter and `origin:`
- falls back to the local file path for `origin:` only when nothing durable can be derived, and says so

## Smaller, independently useful fix

Even without a PDF handler: when `ingest text` is given a path under a temp directory (`/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`), warn that `origin:` is being set to an ephemeral path and suggest passing an explicit origin. A `--origin <url>` flag on `ingest text` would let the caller set it correctly up front instead of patching the committed file afterwards.


========== #188: Entity-resolution 'update' targets a page that exists only on another unmerged ingest branch — silently skipped, so the second source about a topic can never enrich into it ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

Two sources about the same subject were ingested back to back. Each got its own ingest branch and draft PR, per design.

- Source #26 → branch A, PR A. Enrichment created `concepts/<the-page>.md` **on branch A**.
- Source #27 → branch B, PR B. Enrichment correctly resolved the same entity at 0.90 confidence, `central` relevance, action `update`, target `concepts/<the-page>.md`.

But enrich runs against the working tree, which is on `main`, where that page does not exist:

```
Entity resolution
┃ Entity          ┃ Type    ┃ Action ┃ Target                ┃ Conf ┃ Relevance ┃
│ <the entity>    │ concept │ update │ concepts/<the-page>.md│ 0.90 │ central   │

warning: <the entity>: entity resolution says update concepts/<the-page>.md,
but that file doesn't exist on disk — skipped
warning: Source 27 (...): enrichment produced no new page, stub, or update for
any entity — nothing will be written for this source.
Enriched source #27: 0 file(s) written, 15 candidate memories, 5 relationships.
No files were written; nothing to land.
```

Source #27 is now flagged enriched. Its 15 memories exist. But **no page content was written anywhere**, and the second source's genuinely unique material (in this case, author commentary that appears in the secondary source and not the primary) is not in any note.

## Why this is a real design gap, not just my usage

Branch-per-source is wakil's own model, and it is normal to ingest a cluster of related sources in one sitting before reviewing any PRs. In that situation every source after the first that resolves to a page created by an earlier unmerged source silently no-ops. The operator gets two warnings and an exit code of 0.

## Two separable problems

1. **Detection**: entity resolution matched against something (the index? the DB?) that knows about the page, while the writer checks only the working tree. Those two views should agree, or the mismatch should be surfaced as an error rather than a skip.
2. **Recovery**: there is no obvious way to say "apply this to the version on branch A" or "queue this update to reapply after PR A merges". `--force` does not help: nothing was written to update.

## Suggested handling

At minimum, exit non-zero with an actionable message naming the branch that holds the target file, so this doesn't pass as a successful enrichment. Better: detect that the target exists on an open ingest branch and offer to stack onto it, or record a pending update that re-runs after the merge.

## Workaround

None found that stays inside the tool. Landing the first PR before enriching the second source would work, but that inverts the intended review flow (PRs are meant to be reviewed by a human, later, in a batch), and requires knowing in advance which sources will collide.


========== #187: enrich proposes a type: source page under drafts/, which its own validator rejects — whole run hard-fails and writes nothing ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

`wakil enrich 27` ran to completion, produced 15 candidate memories and 5 relationships, then threw the entire result away because the page it had just written for itself violated its own routing rule:

```
Proposed note:
╭─ NEW drafts/techtalks-overview-how-to-build-ai-agents-that-can-handle-th.md ─╮
│ ---
│ title: "How to build AI agents that can handle thousands of tools (TechTalks…"
│ origin: article
│ url: https://bdtechtalks.com
│ ...
│ type: source
│ ---

Proposal failed validation — it cannot be applied:
  ✗ drafts/techtalks-overview-how-to-build-ai-agents-that-can-handle-th.md: type
    'source' pages belong under sources/, not drafts/
Nothing was written. Fix the gap (or re-run enrichment) and try again.
```

## The inconsistency

The proposal generator and the validator disagree about a rule the validator states flatly and mechanically: `type: source` → `sources/`. This is not a judgment call the model needs to get right — it is a pure function of the `type:` field.

Note that enrich **already auto-corrects the filename half** of the path when it disagrees with `slugify()`, emitting a `warning:` and proceeding. It should do the same for the directory half. A deterministic, single-valued correction is being treated as a fatal error instead.

## Expected

Either:

1. Auto-correct the directory from the schema's `directory:` for that `type` and emit a warning (symmetric with the existing slugify filename correction), **or**
2. Constrain generation so the directory is derived from `type` rather than chosen freely.

Failing the whole run and discarding the memories is the worst of the three options.

## Cost of the current behaviour

All model work for the run is wasted; the operator has to re-run enrichment (paying for it twice) and has no lever to fix "the gap" other than guessing at extra `--context` to steer the model away from `drafts/`.

## Workaround used

Re-ran with an explicit `--context` instructing it that `type: source` pages must live under `sources/`. The second run then proposed no page at all (for an unrelated reason — see the sibling issue about entity-resolution targets on other branches).


========== #186: enrich emits two near-duplicate pages for the same entity in a single run when slugify() renames one proposed path ==========
LABELS: bug
## What happened

A single `wakil enrich <id>` run on one source produced **two concept pages describing the same entity**, with byte-identical `name:` and `title:` frontmatter:

```
warning: Corrected the proposed note's filename from
concepts/compositional-skill-routing.md to
concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver.md to match slugify() (the same
convention new entity stub pages already use)
Enriched source #26: 2 file(s) written, 12 candidate memories, 5 relationships.
  + concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver.md
  + concepts/compositional-skill-routing-skillweaver-sad.md
```

Both files carried:

```yaml
type: concept
name: Compositional Skill Routing
title: "Compositional Skill Routing / SKILLWEAVER & SAD"
aliases: [<same four aliases>]
```

They were ~80% overlapping prose — same framework description, same statistics, same open threads, differently worded. Entity resolution had reported a single `create` action for one entity.

## Why it looks like a slugify interaction

The model appears to have proposed two paths for what it considered one entity (a general page and a technique-specific page). The slugify correction then rewrote one of them into a near-neighbour of the other. Whatever the origin, nothing downstream noticed that two proposed pages shared an identical `name:` + `type:` pair before writing both.

## Expected

Before writing, dedupe proposed pages by `(type, name)` — or at minimum by `(type, slugify(name))`. If two proposals collide, merge them or fail loudly. The slugify-correction step in particular should check whether its *corrected* path collides with another path in the same proposal set, since the correction is exactly what can create the collision.

## Impact

Silent duplicate entity pages in the vault, landed on a PR branch with a passing enrichment. Caught only by reading the diff. This is adjacent to but distinct from #170 (duplicates *across* `--force` retries) — this one happens within a single successful run.

## Repro sketch

Ingest a long technical document about one named framework that has a memorable sub-technique (framework X, technique Y), where the natural page title would be "X / Y". Enrich it.


========== #183: No way to delete/archive a source record via CLI or MCP ==========
LABELS: enhancement
## Problem

`wakil sources` (CLI) only exposes `list`, `show`, and `backfill-abstract` —
there's no `delete`/`archive`/`supersede` command. The MCP surface mirrors
this: `sources_list`/`sources_show` only, no mutation beyond
`ingest_apply`/`enrich_apply`.

Concrete case (kb-professional, 2026-08-05): two sources (Engineer B
#20, Engineer A #21/#22 — the latter itself a duplicate from #170) got
corrupted content committed against them during the concurrent-session
interference documented in #181/#182. The GitHub PRs were closable and the
git branches deletable, but the underlying `sources` rows have no supported
way to be marked dead/superseded — they just sit in `wakil sources list`
permanently, with `git_branch`/`git_pr_url` values pointing at branches/PRs
that no longer exist, and no way to distinguish "abandoned, redo happened
under a new source id" from "still needs attention."

## Fix direction

- `wakil sources archive <id> [--reason TEXT] [--superseded-by ID]` (or
  equivalent MCP tool) — soft-delete: keep the row for history but exclude
  it from default `list`/search-adjacent surfaces, and let `show` render an
  "archived, superseded by #N" banner.
- Worth considering whether `ingest_apply`/`enrich_apply` should offer an
  explicit "supersedes source #N" link when re-ingesting the same
  audio/meeting after a prior attempt is known-bad, so the relationship is
  queryable rather than just implied by matching filenames/dates.



========== #182: No isolation between concurrent wakil sessions sharing one working tree — commits/checkouts interleave and clobber uncommitted edits ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

Working on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (kb-professional), I observed clear evidence that a second, independent process was operating against the exact same git working directory and `wakil` SQLite store at the same time as my own session:

1. **Duplicate ingest of the same source.** ~41 seconds after my own `wakil enrich 21 --force` finished, a second `wakil ingest transcript` commit (`7935c2a1`) appeared on a brand-new branch (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-a`, PR #26 in kb-professional), using the *same* scratchpad input file path I had used for my own ingest, and hitting the "-1" filename-collision suffix (#173) against the target path my own earlier ingest had already produced (`sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-transcript-note-engineer-a.md` → `...-1.md`). I never re-ran `wakil ingest transcript` myself. `gh pr list` confirms both PRs are real, both open, both about the same person (Engineer A), created 8 minutes apart.

2. **Uncommitted working-tree content changed under me repeatedly**, mid-task, on files I had just written and had *not yet committed* — e.g. `people/engineer-a.md` and `sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-acme-engineer-a.md` each came back with materially different content (different prose, different timestamps like "Duration: 00:29:21" vs my "00:33:48", different turn boundaries) than what I had just written, with no `git commit` of mine in between. `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` had to be used repeatedly to restore my own committed version before each subsequent commit.

3. **`git branch --show-current` changed without me running `git checkout`.** `git reflog` shows checkouts I did not issue (e.g. `moving from wakil/ingest/...-engineer-a to wakil/ingest/...-with-engineer-a`) interleaved with my own commands.

This points to two (or more) `wakil`-driven agent sessions sharing one on-disk working directory/clone with no isolation (no `git worktree`, no per-session lock), so each session's `git checkout`/`git commit`/file writes are directly visible to and can clobber the other's in-flight, uncommitted work. Anything one session commits and pushes is safe (git objects are immutable), but everything in between — working-tree edits, staged-but-uncommitted state, which branch is currently checked out — is a shared, unguarded resource.

## Fix direction

- If `wakil`'s design intends to support multiple concurrent sessions against one workspace root, each session should operate in its own `git worktree` (or an equivalent per-session clone/checkout) rather than sharing the single working directory that `wakil init` registers.
- Short of that, `wakil ingest`/`enrich` could at least take a lock (e.g. an advisory file lock under `.wakil/`) around the sequence of "checkout branch → write files → commit → return to prior branch," so two invocations can't interleave their checkouts/commits, and could detect "another wakil process appears to be active" and fail fast rather than silently interleaving.
- Worth an explicit note in workspace-level docs (and in any task/orchestration instructions that assume "one agent at a time, exclusive use of the working tree") that this is NOT currently guaranteed by wakil itself — today it's purely a scheduling/discipline convention the caller has to enforce out-of-band.

## Related

kb-professional PR #25 vs PR #26 (both "AI-mentoring 1:1 with Engineer A", same source content, 8 minutes apart) is the concrete duplicate this produced and needs manual reconciliation.



========== #181: enrich commits its changes onto main instead of the source branch, then leaves HEAD on an unrelated stale branch ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

Repro: on branch `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (created by a prior `wakil ingest transcript` run, source #21), ran:

```
wakil enrich 21 --force --yes
```

Output ended with:

```
Enriched source #21: 3 file(s) written, 6 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
  + people/engineer-a.md
  + companies/client-company.md
  + projects/client-company/ai-mentoring/client-company-ai-mentoring-program.md
Committed d437dba430 on wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a
PR: https://github.com/ebridges/kb-professional/pull/25
Returned to wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g.
```

Two things are wrong here, both confirmed via `git log`/`git reflog`/`git branch --contains`:

1. **The commit `d437dba430` actually landed on `main`**, not on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` as the printed message claims. `git branch --contains d437dba430` returned only `main`. Local `main` ended up one commit ahead of `origin/main` (unpushed, luckily, so no bad merge occurred yet) — but this silently commits enrichment output directly onto the trunk, bypassing the PR/branch workflow entirely for anyone who doesn't independently check `git log main` afterward. Recovered by hand: `git cherry-pick d437dba430` onto the correct branch, then `git branch -f main origin/main` to reset the accidental commit off of main.

2. **The "Returned to ..." message checks out a completely unrelated branch** (`...-with-engineer-g`, a different person's in-progress ingest from earlier in the same session) instead of returning to `main` (like `wakil ingest transcript` does) or staying on the branch it just committed to. This leaves the working tree on a random stale branch with no relation to the just-run command, which is confusing and risks the next command in a script operating on the wrong branch.

## Fix direction

- `enrich` should commit onto the same branch the source's capture step created (or the branch that was checked out when `enrich` was invoked), never onto `main` regardless of what branch happens to be checked out when the internal git commit step runs.
- After committing, `enrich` should return to a predictable branch — ideally the branch it just committed on (matching capture step's docstring: "Lands on the same branch/PR the capture step started"), not whatever branch was left checked out by some unrelated prior command in the same shell session.
- Given #170/#168 already document workspace/branch-tracking issues in this area, this may share a root cause — flagging as its own issue since the repro and blast radius (silent commits onto `main`) are distinct and more severe.



========== #180: ingest's PR-landing step resolves the wrong existing branch/PR, causing cross-contamination between unrelated sources ==========
LABELS: bug
## Problem

When `wakil ingest transcript` (or the branch/PR-landing step it shares with
`wakil enrich`) checks whether a PR already exists for the branch it just
created/computed, it appears to resolve an **unrelated** existing branch
rather than doing an exact match against the branch name it just used for
this source. The failure surfaced as a `gh pr create failed: ... already
exists` error citing a branch name that belongs to a completely different,
unrelated source/person.

Downstream, a subsequent `wakil enrich <source_id>` call for the *correct*
source somehow ended up with the repo checked out on that *wrong* branch,
with a different (unrelated) source's uncommitted enrichment output sitting
in the working tree — i.e. this isn't just a cosmetic error message, the
git-branch resolution genuinely diverges from the source's own recorded
`git_branch` DB field at some point in the ingest→enrich flow.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-04, kb-professional vault)

1. `wakil ingest transcript <engineer-b-scratchpad-file>` correctly captured
   source id 20, committed to a correctly-named new branch
   (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w-engineer-b`), but
   then failed at the PR-creation step:

   ```
   Landing failed: gh pr create failed: a pull request for branch
   "wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g" into branch
   "main" already exists:
   https://github.com/ebridges/kb-professional/pull/23
   The written files are still on disk for manual review.
   ```

   Note: `...-with-engineer-b` and `...-with-engineer-g` are unrelated
   branches for unrelated sources/people — there is no reason the
   Engineer B ingest should ever look up or reference the Engineer G
   branch/PR.

2. `wakil sources show 20` correctly reported the source's own `Git branch`
   field as `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w-engine…`
   (the correct branch) — so the DB row itself was not corrupted.

3. Immediately after, running `wakil enrich 20 --force` (which per
   `--help` "lands on the same branch/PR the capture step started") resulted
   in the actual git working tree being checked out on
   `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-g` (the
   *wrong*, unrelated branch), with uncommitted local modifications to
   `companies/the-client-company.md` and `people/engineer-g.md`, plus an
   untracked `sensitive/the-client-company/engineer-g-ai-mentoring-assessment.md`
   — content that clearly belongs to a completely different source's
   enrichment output, not source 20's.

   (Caveat: a second, genuinely concurrent Claude Code session was also
   active against this same working directory/repo during this window, so
   it's possible the two symptoms above have partially independent causes —
   but the branch-name string cited in the PR-creation error in step 1 is
   real evidence of a wakil-side resolution bug regardless, since that
   error occurred on the very first `ingest` invocation before any
   possibility of a second session's git operations being involved.)

## Fix direction

Whatever code path does the "does a PR already exist for this branch"
check before calling `gh pr create` should look up by **exact** branch
name (the one just written to the source's own `git_branch` DB column),
not by a fuzzy/prefix/title-similarity match that can collide with a
different branch whose auto-generated name happens to share a long common
prefix (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-w...` in this
case). Given the collision-prone naming scheme (dates + truncated titles),
an exact-match bug here is likely to keep recurring across this vault's
current heavy one-person-per-branch ingest workload.

301	========== #182: No isolation between concurrent wakil sessions sharing one working tree — commits/checkouts interleave and clobber uncommitted edits ==========
302	LABELS: bug
303	## Problem
304	
305	Working on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (kb-professional), I observed clear evidence that a second, independent process was operating against the exact same git working directory and `wakil` SQLite store at the same time as my own session:
306	
307	1. **Duplicate ingest of the same source.** ~41 seconds after my own `wakil enrich 21 --force` finished, a second `wakil ingest transcript` commit (`7935c2a1`) appeared on a brand-new branch (`wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-with-engineer-a`, PR #26 in kb-professional), using the *same* scratchpad input file path I had used for my own ingest, and hitting the "-1" filename-collision suffix (#173) against the target path my own earlier ingest had already produced (`sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-transcript-note-engineer-a.md` → `...-1.md`). I never re-ran `wakil ingest transcript` myself. `gh pr list` confirms both PRs are real, both open, both about the same person (Engineer A), created 8 minutes apart.
308	
309	2. **Uncommitted working-tree content changed under me repeatedly**, mid-task, on files I had just written and had *not yet committed* — e.g. `people/engineer-a.md` and `sources/transcripts/2026-08-04-acme-engineer-a.md` each came back with materially different content (different prose, different timestamps like "Duration: 00:29:21" vs my "00:33:48", different turn boundaries) than what I had just written, with no `git commit` of mine in between. `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` had to be used repeatedly to restore my own committed version before each subsequent commit.
310	
311	3. **`git branch --show-current` changed without me running `git checkout`.** `git reflog` shows checkouts I did not issue (e.g. `moving from wakil/ingest/...-engineer-a to wakil/ingest/...-with-engineer-a`) interleaved with my own commands.
312	
313	This points to two (or more) `wakil`-driven agent sessions sharing one on-disk working directory/clone with no isolation (no `git worktree`, no per-session lock), so each session's `git checkout`/`git commit`/file writes are directly visible to and can clobber the other's in-flight, uncommitted work. Anything one session commits and pushes is safe (git objects are immutable), but everything in between — working-tree edits, staged-but-uncommitted state, which branch is currently checked out — is a shared, unguarded resource.
314	
315	## Fix direction
316	
317	- If `wakil`'s design intends to support multiple concurrent sessions against one workspace root, each session should operate in its own `git worktree` (or an equivalent per-session clone/checkout) rather than sharing the single working directory that `wakil init` registers.
318	- Short of that, `wakil ingest`/`enrich` could at least take a lock (e.g. an advisory file lock under `.wakil/`) around the sequence of "checkout branch → write files → commit → return to prior branch," so two invocations can't interleave their checkouts/commits, and could detect "another wakil process appears to be active" and fail fast rather than silently interleaving.
319	- Worth an explicit note in workspace-level docs (and in any task/orchestration instructions that assume "one agent at a time, exclusive use of the working tree") that this is NOT currently guaranteed by wakil itself — today it's purely a scheduling/discipline convention the caller has to enforce out-of-band.
320	
321	## Related
322	
323	kb-professional PR #25 vs PR #26 (both "AI-mentoring 1:1 with Engineer A", same source content, 8 minutes apart) is the concrete duplicate this produced and needs manual reconciliation.

330	
331	Repro: on branch `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` (created by a prior `wakil ingest transcript` run, source #21), ran:
332	
333	```
334	wakil enrich 21 --force --yes
335	```
336	
337	Output ended with:
338	
339	```
340	Enriched source #21: 3 file(s) written, 6 candidate memories, 3 relationships.
341	  + people/engineer-a.md
342	  + companies/client-company.md
343	  + projects/client-company/ai-mentoring/client-company-ai-mentoring-program.md
344	Committed d437dba430 on wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a
345	PR: https://github.com/ebridges/kb-professional/pull/25

347	```
348	
349	Two things are wrong here, both confirmed via `git log`/`git reflog`/`git branch --contains`:
350	
351	1. **The commit `d437dba430` actually landed on `main`**, not on `wakil/ingest/2026-08-04-2026-08-04-ai-mentoring-1-1-engineer-a` as the printed message claims. `git branch --contains d437dba430` returned only `main`. 356	
357	- `enrich` should commit onto the same branch the source's capture step created (or the branch that was checked out when `enrich` was invoked), never onto `main` regardless of what branch happens to be checked out when the internal git commit step runs.
358	- After committing, `enrich` should return to a predictable branch — ideally the branch it just committed on (matching capture step's docstring: "Lands on the same branch/PR the capture step started"), not whatever branch was left checked out by some unrelated prior command in the same shell session.

449	already-authored prose to pass through unchanged.

546	LABELS: bug
547	## Problem
548	
549	Two separate synthesis-accuracy observations from `wakil enrich`'s generated content this session — neither is a hard crash/wrong-file-write bug, both are content-quality issues worth a look, filing together since they're both about the enrichment LLM pass's care with facts already present in its own input.
550	
551	### 1. Claimed content was "not present in the transcript" when it was
552	
553	`wakil enrich`'s auto-generated meeting-note summary for a source included:
554	
555	> "The provided transcript excerpt ends mid-discussion; the recording's own abstract references a back-office / data-ingestion database as the area hardest to pick up cold, but that segment is not present in the captured transcript here."
556

561	I guess it's the part for the actual database of this core system right now for the back office platform.
562	
563	### [26:28] John Doe
564	Because as far as I know, that thing is a mess at the moment.
565	
566	### [26:39] John Doe
567	Yeah, and the entire how they store it in those thousands of duplicates, under duplicates of duplicates.
568	```
569	
570	i.e. the whole transcript was in the file being enriched, but the model asserted a specific true fact about its own input was absent — worth checking whether whatever context window/chunking `enrich` uses is truncating the source before the synthesis step sees the end of a ~415-segment / 28-minute transcript.

572	### 2. Enrichment defaults to "he/him" for a person entity when nothing in the source specifies gender

574	Enriching a source for `[[people/joe-doe]]` produced Compiled Truth / Timeline prose using he/him pronouns throughout ("his tenure", "He gave concrete... examples", etc). ========== #171 ==========
TITLE: wakil enrich/ingest's internal git commit has a ~60s timeout too short for interactive signing (SSH/1Password)
## Problem

The `git commit` step inside `wakil ingest`/`wakil enrich`'s "landing" flow (branch → write files → commit → push → open/flip PR) appears to have a hardcoded timeout around 60 seconds. When the commit takes longer than that — e.g. because the repo's commits are SSH-signed via a hardware key or 1Password, which pops an interactive approval prompt — the whole operation fails partway through, leaving written files uncommitted on disk and the source's git-landing state inconsistent.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-04, kb-professional vault, source #13 "1:1 with Engineer D")

```
Enriched source #13: 3 file(s) written, 22 candidate memories, 7 relationships.
  + people/engineer-d.md
  + companies/the-client-company.md
  + projects/the-client-company/ai-mentoring/the-client-company-mentoring-engagement-plan.md
Review files with git diff/status; review memories with `wakil memory list --state candidate`.
Landing failed: git commit failed: Command '['git', '-C', '/Users/ebridges/Projects/kb-professional', 'commit', '-m', "...", '--', 'people/engineer-d.md', 'companies/the-client-company.md', 'projects/the-client-company/ai-mentoring/the-client-company-mentoring-engagement-plan.md']' timed out after 60 seconds
The written files are still on disk for manual review.
```

The repo's commits require SSH-signing approval (1Password), which routinely takes longer than 60s to be interactively approved by a human. Every other successful `wakil` commit in the same session took anywhere from a few seconds to ~a minute depending on how quickly the signing prompt was approved — 60s is well within normal variance for this setup, not a hang.

Recovery required manually running the same `git commit` (with a much longer timeout) myself, then manually `git push`ing and `git checkout main`ing, since the tool had already reported failure and abandoned the branch mid-flow.

## Fix direction

- Don't impose a short hardcoded timeout on a `git commit` invocation that may need to wait on an interactive credential/signing prompt — either make it configurable (e.g. `--commit-timeout`), or default to something much longer (5-10 min) given this is explicitly a human-in-the-loop operation, or detect that stdin/stdout are a TTY and skip the timeout entirely in that case.
- On timeout/failure, leave the working tree in a resumable state (branch checked out, files staged) rather than requiring the caller to reconstruct the commit message and manually push/return-to-main by hand.

========== #170 ==========
TITLE: enrich --force retries duplicate a draft page instead of updating the one from the previous retry
## Problem

When `wakil enrich <id> --force` is re-run because a prior run's entity resolution failed to find/update the real target pages (see #168 — likely root cause), each retry creates a **new, differently-named draft page** instead of recognizing and updating the page the previous retry already created. There's no de-dup against the enrichment's *own* prior output on the same source.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-03, kb-professional vault, source #14 "Engineer E AI-mentoring 1:1")

Three consecutive `wakil enrich 14 --force --yes` runs (each preceded by a fresh `wakil init`, each hitting the #168-style "file doesn't exist on disk" failure) produced **six files** for what should have been one canonical assessment page:

```
sensitive/engineer-e-ai-mentoring-assessment.md
sensitive/the-client-company/engineer-e-ai-mentoring-assessment.md
sensitive/engineer-e-ai-mentoring-assessment-the-client-company.md
sensitive/the-client-company/engineer-e-ai-mentoring-assessment-the-client-company.md
sensitive/engineer-e-assessment-the-client-company-ai-mentoring.md
sensitive/the-client-company/ai-mentoring/engineer-e-assessment-the-client-company-ai-mentoring.md
```

Each of the three runs produced genuinely different prose (different titles, different frontmatter shapes — one run included a `title:` field the others omitted, tag ordering differed, one used wikilinked `subject:`/`company:` values and another used plain strings) — i.e. this isn't a byte-identical re-write being saved under a new name, it's a **full independent re-synthesis** each time, with no awareness of its own prior attempt.

Also notable: **within a single run**, two files were written for the same content — one at a flat `sensitive/<slug>.md` path and one at a nested `sensitive/the-client-company/<slug>.md` path. That looks like a separate routing issue (writing to two candidate paths in one apply) worth its own look, distinct from the cross-run duplication above.

This has the same *shape* as #36 (duplicate entity files from extraction + entity-resolution not reconciled) but a different trigger: #36 was about extraction and entity-resolution disagreeing within a single run; this is about **repeated `--force` runs on the same source** never recognizing a page that a *previous run of the same command* already created.

## Fix direction

Before creating a new page for an entity-resolution `create` target, check whether a page already exists that's linked to this same `source_id` (e.g. via the source's git history / a `source:` or backlink frontmatter field, or by checking recent commits on the source's own ingest branch) and treat that as an `update` target instead of a fresh `create`, even when the live entity-resolution pass itself can't currently resolve the canonical page path (e.g. due to #168). This would make `--force` retries idempotent even while the underlying disk-visibility bug is being fixed.

========== #168 ==========
TITLE: [Workspace identity] Path-based root_path matching breaks under symlink/mv/duplicate-checkout
## Problem

`Workspace` row identity in `wakil.db` is keyed on an exact-string
`root_path` match (`_ensure_workspace` in `app/workspace_service.py`),
compared against whatever `find_workspace_root()` resolves for the
current invocation. `find_workspace_root()` always calls `.resolve()`,
which dereferences symlinks. So if the same physical repo is ever
reachable via two different literal path strings — a symlink alias, a
second clone, a different mount point, a renamed directory whose old
`.wakil/config.yaml` still has stale state — `wakil` cannot recognize
them as the same workspace. Depending on how it's invoked, it either
fails with `Unknown workspace: <name>` or silently creates a second,
parallel `workspaces` row, fragmenting that repo's sources/memories/
notes/relationships across two untraceable identities.

Compounding this: `wakil init --name X` silently overwrites
`.wakil/config.yaml`'s `name:` field when the target directory is
already initialized under a different name, with no warning — the
proximate trigger for the incident below.

## Worked example (2026-07-31, `kb-professional` vault)

- `~/Projects/kb-professional` was a symlink to `~/Projects/kb`, created
  2026-07-28. Before that date, `kb-professional` was a real, separately
  registered workspace (`id=1`, name `professional`, `root_path=".../kb-
  professional"`, history back to 2026-07-09).
- After the symlink was introduced, no invocation could ever again
  produce the literal string `.../kb-professional` — `.resolve()` always
  collapsed it to `.../kb`. Workspace `id=1` became permanently
  unreachable by name or path, silently.
- A later session, hitting `Unknown workspace: kb`, ran
  `wakil init ~/Projects/kb --name kb` per this vault's own documented
  recovery instructions ("safe to re-run, never destroys data"). This
  created workspace `id=2` (`root_path=".../kb"`) — a second row for the
  same physical repo — rather than fixing `id=1`'s identity.
- Net effect: `id=1`'s data (7 sources, 91 memories, full note/
  relationship index, ~3 weeks of history) went silently untouched but
  unreachable, while `id=2` started from zero. Nothing errored at any
  point. Diagnosis required directly querying the SQLite tables and
  reading `workspace_service.py`/`config/registry.py`/`config/settings.py`
  to understand the resolution chain.
- Recovery required a manual SQL transaction (repoint sources/memories/
  git_changes/ingest_runs and memory-linked relationships from `id=2` to
  `id=1`; delete `id=2`'s redundant re-derived notes/relationships rows;
  delete the `id=2` workspace row) followed by physically renaming the
  symlinked directory into a real one so `id=1`'s stored `root_path`
  became reachable again.

## Proposed fix

1. **Add a stable local anchor.** Generate a UUID into
   `.wakil/config.yaml` the first time a workspace is initialized
   (`workspace_id: <uuid>`, alongside `name`/`root_path`). Because this
   file lives *inside* the directory being identified, it survives
   `mv`/rename for free. Add a matching nullable `external_id` column to
   the `workspaces` table.

2. **Match on that anchor first, path second.** In `_ensure_workspace`,
   look up by `external_id` when present; fall back to the current
   `root_path`-equality lookup only for pre-migration workspaces
   (backfilling `external_id` once found). On every successful match,
   unconditionally overwrite the row's `root_path` to the current
   resolved path — `WorkspaceConfig.load` already does exactly this
   "trust the current invocation" pattern for `root_path`/`state_root`,
   so this extends an existing convention rather than inventing a new
   one. A `mv` or symlink change then becomes a complete non-event.

3. **Use `git_remote` as a secondary consistency signal.** It's already
   captured on every `Workspace` row but never used for identity. When a
   workspace is matched/created and its `git_remote` matches an
   *existing, different* row's `git_remote`, that's exactly this
   incident's failure mode (the same repo registered twice under
   different local paths/names) — surface a warning ("this repo is
   already registered as workspace '{other.name}' at {other.root_path};
   did you mean `-w {other.name}`?") instead of silently duplicating.

4. **Make `wakil init --name X` non-destructive on a name conflict.**
   Once (1)-(2) land, re-initializing an existing directory under a new
   name becomes a safe, well-defined "rename this row in place" (matched
   by `external_id`) rather than a silent, undetected overwrite.

## Also worth fixing

The CLI's error/recovery messaging ("safe to re-run... never destroys
data") is accurate for the common case but not for this one — worth
softening or caveating until the above lands.

=== DEVELOPMENT.md ===
---
title: Development Patterns
status: living
audience: wakil design

# Development Patterns

## About

Recurring dev conventions worth generalizing to future, different work — not
a changelog and not a place for one-off fixes. An entry only belongs here if
the pattern should apply beyond the change that established it. Most work
sessions should add nothing; see the `development-docs` skill
(`.claude/skills/development-docs/SKILL.md`) for the judgment process that maintains
this file. Every entry cites a concrete source (commit SHA, PR #, or session
detail) for traceability.

### Split error handling around a git-landing step

**Source:** PR #15 (`worktree-git-integration` branch), `src/wakil/cli/main.py`

When a command lands on a branch (`prepare_landing`) before doing risked work (e.g. `apply_capture`/`apply_enrichment`), catch the landing call's `GitServiceError` in its own `try` block, separate from the subsequent operation's errors. On any failure in the operation after a successful landing, call `abandon_landing(config, landing)` so the worktree returns to its own branch instead of being left stranded on the throwaway ingest branch. `enrich` established this shape first (commit `f5a4ed1`); `_run_ingest` originally wrapped `prepare_landing` and `apply_capture` in one combined `try` block, and was split to match `enrich` in commit `a14af48`, whose message describes closing the gap this way: "so a race loss returns the session to its original branch via abandon_landing instead of stranding it on the throwaway ingest branch."

Note: as of this writing PR #15 is still an open draft (unmerged into `main`); this pattern applies once/if that branch lands.

### Run the live eval before treating new SKILL.md guidance as done

**Source:** PR #20 (`docs/skill-guidance-for-linked-context` branch), `src/wakil/skills/entity-enrichment/SKILL.md`

Adding a new rule to a skill's SKILL.md and a matching `eval.json` scenario for it isn't finished until `uv run pytest -m eval -k <scenario id>` (a real model call, per `docs/adr/0004`) actually passes — prose that reads correct to a human reviewer can still be misapplied by the model in a way only a live run surfaces. Here, a new rule said an explicit `@file:` reference should be treated as "high-confidence" for back-linking; the model read that confidence as also covering content-worthiness and appended a Timeline entry for a mention the source said had nothing new to report, failing the eval's rubric. The fix was one clarifying sentence separating the link decision from the content decision — but the gap was invisible without actually running the eval. When adding or editing skill guidance, write (or extend) its `eval.json` scenario and run it live before considering the change done, not just at merge/CI time.

### A skill's `references/*.md` files are never loaded into the model's context

**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, live-eval triage session, 2026-07-21

`load_skill()` (`src/wakil/llm/skill_loader.py`) builds `skill.body` from `SKILL.md` alone — nothing inlines a skill's `references/*.md` files, even though several SKILL.md files (`source-ingestion`, `skill-authoring`) point at them for what reads as load-bearing judgment ("see `references/source-types.md` for the per-source-type judgment"). This is true both in `wakil enrich`'s real pipeline (`build_system_prompt`) and the eval harness (`run_scenario`) — a human reading the skill file would follow the pointer and find the guidance; the model never does, regardless of how clearly SKILL.md cites the file. Two separate live-eval failures (a fabricated YouTube-transcription workaround, a promotion checklist the model never applied) traced to this exact cause. When a SKILL.md cites a `references/` file for guidance that actually needs to affect model behavior (not just serve as a longer human-readable writeup), pull the load-bearing part into `SKILL.md`'s own body — `references/` can still carry the fuller version, but the file itself must not be the only place the instruction lives.

### Check whether a skill's own procedure step order can produce the bug it's trying to prevent

**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, `note-routing/SKILL.md`, 2026-07-21

`note-routing`'s decision tree had "generate the filename" as Step 5 and "surface ambiguity, don't pick" as Step 6 — so a model following the numbered steps in order committed to a filename before ever reaching the ambiguity check the later step was supposed to gate. The instruction to "surface ambiguity" was correct in isolation; the bug was purely in where it sat relative to the step it needed to precede. When a skill's procedure is a numbered sequence and a later step is meant to be a conditional gate on an earlier one, check that the gate actually comes first — a correct rule stated too late in the list doesn't prevent the thing it names.

### Print diagnostic detail as it happens, not deferred to a final summary

**Source:** `fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps` branch, `scripts/classify_eval_failures.py` and `uv run pytest -m eval -v` runs, 2026-07-21/22

Two separate long-running eval scripts in this session lost their most important output to the same mistake: accumulating results in memory and only printing the useful summary (pytest's failure list, this script's per-item failure reasons) at the very end of the run. `scripts/classify_eval_failures.py` hit a live-model API usage cap partway through a 10-scenario classification pass and crashed — the log had per-scenario pass/fail counts but none of the actual failing rubric items or grader reasons, because those were only assembled into the final `CLASSIFICATION TABLE` the crash never reached. Fixed by printing each individual grading result (pass/fail, failed item, grader reason) immediately as it happens, keeping the end-of-run table as a convenience recap rather than the only place the detail lives. For any script making a sequence of live model calls with real cost/failure risk, print the thing you'd actually need to read *at the point each result arrives*, not after the loop — a partial run should still be a useful run.

### Zip a vendored data file, document its source in a sibling `.SOURCE.md`

**Source:** PR #21 (`refactor/candidate-notes-stopword-filtering` branch), `src/wakil/app/data/`

When vendoring a third-party data file (a word list, a static lookup table) into the repo, zip it rather than committing plain text — `common_words.zip` is 17KB against the original 34KB `common_words.txt`, decompressed once at import time via the stdlib `zipfile` module, not re-read per call. Because a zip's contents aren't reviewable in a plain `git diff`, add a sibling `<name>.SOURCE.md` documenting where the data came from, its license, and how to regenerate/refresh it — `common_words.SOURCE.md` is the template to copy for the next one.

### A full live-model eval-suite run has a high baseline failure rate — don't read it as a regression signal

**Source:** session comparing `uv run pytest -m eval -q` across PRs #21-#24 and `main`, 2026-07-21

Running the complete `-m eval` suite (all skill scenarios, not a single targeted scenario) produced roughly 45-53% failures on every branch tested, including ~16-17 of 47 scenarios that failed identically across branches with zero code overlap (SCHEMA.md removal, capture-time model calls, candidate-filtering, related-notes search — none of which share a code path). Every unique-to-one-branch failure spot-checked was the same character of failure: a subjective "did the model stay strictly within its stated skill boundary" or "did it avoid inventing a disambiguating detail" rubric item, not a functional break. This matches `docs/adr/0004`'s own rationale for excluding these from the required CI gate. Before treating a full-suite eval run's failures as evidence of a regression, compare against a same-day `main` baseline (or re-run the specific failing scenario in isolation) rather than reading the raw failure count at face value — a targeted, single-scenario eval run (e.g. verifying one new rubric item after a SKILL.md wording change) is a much more reliable signal than a full-suite sweep.

### An ADR's `status: accepted` means the decision was made, not that it was implemented

**Source:** `docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md`, 2026-07-23

ADR 0006 ("Backlinks as a Live Query Over a Widened Relationship Table") is `status: accepted` and its schema/migration exist, but grepping the real application code turned up exactly one place a `Relationship` row is ever constructed (`ingest_service.py`'s `apply_enrichment`) — and it only ever writes `subject_memory_id`/`object_memory_id`. The note-note columns the ADR is about (`subject_note_id`/`object_note_id`) are populated nowhere in the real pipeline, exercised only by one hand-constructed unit test roundtrip. This wasn't caught until a downstream consumer (a kb-side skill assuming backlinks were already automatic) went looking for the actual write path. Before citing an accepted ADR's decision as current, working behavior in a new design doc, a docstring, or downstream documentation, grep for where it's actually implemented — `status: accepted` records that a decision was made, not that every consequence of it landed in code.

### Diarized transcript formats each get their own `parse_<x>_transcript()` sharing one merge helper

**Source:** `fix/json-transcript-diarization` branch, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, 2026-07-25

A plain-JSON transcript export (`{"segments": [{"speaker": "Speaker 1", "text": ..., "start": ...}]}`) looked like the same shape as an Apple `.whisper` zip archive's `metadata.json` (`{"transcripts": [{"speaker": {"name": ...}, ...}]}`) but wasn't — different container (zip vs. plain file), different top-level key (`transcripts` vs. `segments`), different speaker shape (object vs. flat string) — so it fell through `prepare_capture`'s generic text branch and captured as a raw, undiarized JSON blob instead of dialogue. The fix factored the actual merge logic (consecutive-same-speaker turns, filler-word stripping) out of `parse_whisper_transcript` into a shared `_dialogue_from_segments(segments, speaker_of)` helper, then added `parse_json_transcript()` as a second, format-specific caller. The next new diarized export shape (a different ASR tool's JSON, an SRT-with-speaker-labels variant, etc.) should follow the same shape: a small `parse_<x>_transcript()` that extracts its own `segments` list and a `speaker_of` callable, gated on file suffix/content in `prepare_capture`, reusing `_dialogue_from_segments` rather than re-implementing the merge.

### Anthropic prompt caching needs an identical prefix through `system` too, not just a matching shared block

**Established:** 2026-07-25 · **Source:** commit 6b64a5a, `src/wakil/llm/client.py`, `ModelClient.complete()`'s `cacheable_prefix` param

Marking a block with `cache_control` only produces a cache hit if everything before it in the request — `system` included — is byte-identical to a previous call within the TTL. `build_system_prompt` (`skill_loader.py`) bakes each DAG stage's skill body + JSON schema into `system`, so the extraction/resolution/revision calls in one `wakil enrich` run never share a cache lineage even though they all send the same source document — their `system` differs first, breaking the prefix chain before it ever reaches the shared content. `cacheable_prefix` on `ModelClient.complete()` therefore only pays off *within* one call type (retries, and any future batched sub-calls of the same call), never *across* call types, unless `system` itself is made call-invariant — which has its own cost (skill/schema content would move into the user message, a weaker instruction-following position). Before assuming a shared block will cache across two different call sites, check whether their `system` is actually identical first.

### `thinking.budget_tokens` doesn't exist on `claude-opus-4-8` and later — use `output_config.effort` or `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` instead

**Established:** 2026-07-25 · **Source:** `docs/adr/0015-relevance-gated-entities-and-truncation-driven-batching.md` (Decision 2, Step A), `src/wakil/llm/client.py`'s `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`

`AnthropicClient.complete` hardcodes `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}` with no way to bound how much of `max_tokens` thinking consumes before output starts. The obvious lever — `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` — returns a 400 error on `claude-opus-4-8` (this codebase's `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) and every later model in the family (Opus 4.7+, Fable 5, Mythos 5), confirmed against Anthropic's live migration guide (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/migration-guide.md) and not just assumed. The two levers that are actually available on this model, confirmed against the installed SDK's type stubs (`anthropic` package, `types/output_config_param.py`, `types/thinking_config_disabled_param.py`): `output_config={"effort": "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max"}` (compatible with adaptive thinking, currently never set — the call runs at whatever server-side default applies), and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` (eliminates thinking-token cost entirely, at the cost of whatever quality adaptive thinking buys). Before adding a `budget_tokens` cap to any Anthropic call in this codebase, check the current model's actual capability — model-specific thinking/effort support changes across the Claude model lineage, and a docs page is one step removed from observed behavior, so verify with a live call before relying on either lever in production.

### An entity-revision candidate's `content` is one shared in-memory value across prompt, merge, and stale-guard — trace all three before changing what it holds

**Established:** 2026-07-25 · **Source:** ADR 0016 review (rejected "gated context-trimming" design), `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`

`_run_entity_updates` reads each candidate's target-note content exactly once into a `content` string (part of the `_EntityCandidate` tuple), and that same in-memory value is reused three separate times downstream: as the model prompt's input (`_revise_candidates`), as the merge's `old_content` (`_apply_entity_revisions`, `by_path.get(...)`), and as the comparison baseline for `apply_enrichment`'s stale-file guard (`update.old_content`, checked against a fresh disk read at apply time). Nothing re-reads the file between prepare and apply. An ADR proposing to trim that string for just the prompt (to cut context cost) initially claimed the merge step was unaffected because it "always re-reads the full file at apply time" — checked against the actual code, it doesn't; the claim was simply wrong, and acting on it would have silently broken the stale-guard (a trimmed string can never match a fresh full read), the merge (no Timeline heading left for `_TIMELINE_HEADING_RE` to find), and `_split_candidates_by_content_length`'s cost-balancing (which sizes candidates by `len(content)`) all at once, for exactly the notes the change was meant to help. Before changing what a shared value like this holds for one consumer, grep for every other place that same variable/field is read, not just the one motivating the change.

### Known issue: `_resolve_entity_slug` silently picks a winner on a cross-type slug collision

**Source:** PR #33 (`feat/entity-compile-pilot` branch), `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, session discussion 2026-07-26

`_resolve_entity_slug(config, slug)` (backing `wakil entities compile SLUG`) searches every entity type's canonical directory, sorted alphabetically, for a file named `<slug>.md`, and returns the first match — its own docstring says "only one page per slug is expected to exist in practice," but nothing enforces that. If two entities of different types ever share a slug (e.g. a person and a company both slugifying to `edward-bridges`), the resolver silently returns whichever directory sorts first (`companies` before `people`, alphabetically) with no error and no indication a second match exists. The only mitigating factor is that the preview step shows the full resolved path before the user confirms — but nothing actively flags the ambiguity, so an inattentive confirm could compile the wrong entity. Not yet fixed. The intended fix, if picked up: keep the bare-slug ergonomics for the (overwhelmingly common) unambiguous case, but have `_resolve_entity_slug` detect a match in more than one directory and raise a clear error listing every match, directing the user to a full relative path instead of silently guessing — the same "surface ambiguity, don't pick" discipline `note-routing/SKILL.md` already applies to filename generation (see the entry above on step ordering).

### Adding a mandatory model call to the enrichment DAG means auditing every `FakeClient(...)` construction, not just bumping a default

**Established:** 2026-07-27 · **Source:** issue #70, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`'s `_synthesize_stub_content`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py`

`prepare_enrichment`'s DAG (extraction → entity-resolution → entity-updates → …) is exercised almost entirely through `FakeClient`, a fixed-length scripted-response queue with no notion of "this call is optional" — each test's list length has to exactly match however many real model calls that specific resolution shape triggers. Adding a new *unconditional* call partway through the DAG (here: synthesize content for every create-resolution's stub once it survives suppression) broke every test whose fixture happened to produce that condition, not just the ones that explicitly asserted a call count — including tests using the bare default `FakeClient()` and tests with an explicit 2-3-item list built for the DAG shape *before* the new call existed. There is no shortcut around this: bumping `FakeClient.__init__`'s default queue only covers bare `FakeClient()` callers; every explicit-list construction still has to be individually re-derived (does this resolution's create survive suppression? does an update-candidate's target file exist on disk?) and given one more scripted response, or the test fails opaquely with "FakeClient ran out of scripted responses" rather than a clear diff. When adding a new call to this (or any other) fixed-length-fake-backed DAG, budget time to grep every construction site of the fake client, not just its default, before trusting a green test run.

### Stacked same-file refactor PRs from a shared base conflict on sequential merge even when the functions they touch don't overlap

**Established:** 2026-07-30 · **Source:** PRs #109, #110, #111 (three independent function-level refactors of `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, each branched from the same pre-refactor commit)

Three worktree-agent PRs each extracted helpers from a *different* function in `ingest_service.py` (`apply_enrichment`, `_build_stub_entities`, `validate_proposal`), with no line ranges in common. Merging the first two into `main` sequentially was a clean fast-forward, but the third (`validate_proposal`) then failed `gh pr merge` with a conflict, because git's diff anchors on the *text* around a change, not on which named function it belongs to — once `apply_enrichment`'s body was replaced by a call to its new helpers on `main`, the region immediately following the still-unrefactored (from that branch's point of view) `validate_proposal` no longer matched what the `validate_proposal` branch expected to find there, even though neither PR touched the other's actual function body. Rebasing the trailing branch onto the new `main` reproduces the same conflict (it's not merge-order-specific); resolving it requires re-deriving the intended final file — start from `main`'s current version of the file and manually re-apply just the extracted-function's diff, rather than trying to hand-resolve `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` markers in place, since the marked regions don't line up with either branch's actual intended change. When queuing multiple same-file refactor PRs from one audit, expect this on any PR after the first that touches that file, and budget for a manual reconciliation pass rather than a routine merge.

### MCP tools live in `mcp/tools.py` as plain functions; `mcp/server.py` wraps them in closures for FastMCP registration

**Established:** 2026-07-28 · **Source:** `docs/adr/0018-mcp-interface.md`, `src/wakil/mcp/tools.py`/`server.py`

FastMCP's `@mcp.tool()` decorator introspects the wrapped function's signature to build the tool's client-facing JSON schema — any parameter present on that function becomes something the MCP client is expected to supply. Every wakil MCP tool needs a `WorkspaceConfig` (and the write tools need the shared `ProposalCache`) that must stay fixed for the life of one `wakil mcp serve` process, not be re-supplied per call, so those can't be plain parameters on the decorated function. `mcp/tools.py` holds the actual logic as ordinary functions taking `config`/`cache` explicitly first, directly unit-testable with no running server (`tests/unit/test_mcp_tools.py` calls them with no MCP machinery at all); `mcp/server.py`'s `build_server(config)` builds one `ProposalCache`, then registers a thin closure per tool that captures `config`/`cache` and forwards only the remaining, client-facing parameters. The next new MCP tool should follow the same split — logic in `tools.py`, a same-named closure wrapper in `server.py` — rather than writing logic directly inside a `@mcp.tool()`-decorated function.

### A `FakeClient`'s strict queue order stops being reliable once two of its calls run on separate threads

**Established:** 2026-08-03 · **Source:** `docs/adr/0020-enrich-progress-visibility-concurrency-and-checkpointing.md` (Decision 2), `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py`'s `FakeClient`

`prepare_enrichment`'s DAG nodes 3 and 4 (`_run_entity_updates`/`_synthesize_stub_content`) now run concurrently via a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and both share the exact same contract (`EntityRevisionOutput`) and system prompt — indistinguishable to a scripted fake except by which one calls `complete()` first, which thread scheduling now decides rather than the DAG's own code order. Any test that scripted both calls into one `FakeClient([...])` queue and asserted something about a *specific* one of them (its prompt content, or a response tailored to one call but not the other) is flaky under this change, even though the test never mentions threads. `FakeClient` gained an optional `router` param — a list of `(prompt-substring, response)` pairs checked before the queue on every `complete()` call — so a test can pin a specific response to whichever call's prompt contains a target note path unique to it (revision targets and synthesis targets never overlap), while leaving the other call to draw from the plain queue. When adding concurrency between two DAG calls that share a contract, grep every existing scripted-fake test that exercises both calls in one run before trusting a green suite — a call-order assumption baked into fixture data doesn't show up as a diff anyone reviews.

### `EnrichmentCheckpoint` persists each `wakil enrich` DAG phase; a crash or failed `validate_proposal` is not always a full redo

**Established:** 2026-08-03 · **Source:** `docs/adr/0020-enrich-progress-visibility-concurrency-and-checkpointing.md` (Decision 3), `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`

Before assuming a killed/crashed `wakil enrich` run — or one that failed `validate_proposal` for a reason unrelated to any of its 4 model calls — always means starting over: check for `EnrichmentCheckpoint` rows for that source first (`sqlite3 <workspace>/wakil.db 'select phase, created_at from enrichment_checkpoints where source_id = N'`). Each of `prepare_enrichment`'s 4 phases (extraction, resolution, revision, synthesis) is checkpointed on clean completion, keyed by `sha256(source.content_hash | context_digest | model)` — a re-invocation with the same key skips straight past any phase with a matching row. Only clean completions are cached, never a model-call failure (extraction/resolution's `ModelContractError` branches skip the save so a transient failure stays retriable), and only `--force` or a successful `apply_enrichment` ever clears them — a declined preview or a failed `validate_proposal` leaves them in place deliberately. `_build_stub_entities` itself is never checkpointed (only its input, `entity_resolutions`, is) — it always re-runs fresh from whatever resolutions end up on the proposal, so it can't drift between a live and a resumed run.

### Git worktrees fix the ingest lock race, but wakil's workspace identity isn't worktree-aware

**Context:** During work on PR #15, testing showed that two simultaneous `wakil ingest` calls against one shared checkout reliably fail: both call `prepare_landing()` → `git switch -c <branch>`, and one process loses the race for `.git/index.lock` every time (every trial in that test). The user then asked, proactively and hypothetically: "what if each ingest is done on a separate worktree — would that allow them to be operated on in parallel?" That question prompted the investigation below; it was not a reported bug.

**Finding:** Separate git worktrees do solve the lock race — each linked worktree has its own index file, so `git switch`/`git add`/`git commit` in worktree-a and worktree-b don't contend for the same `.git/index.lock`. Across roughly 10 trials of concurrent ingest using two real `git worktree`-created checkouts, no lock collision occurred.

But that alone doesn't make worktrees safe to use, because wakil's own database isn't worktree-aware. `_ensure_workspace()` in `src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py` (main, lines 96–110) looks up the `Workspace` row with an exact string match on `config.root_path`:

```python
workspace = session.scalar(
    select(Workspace).where(Workspace.root_path == str(config.root_path))
)
```

Since each linked worktree is a different directory, the first touch from a second worktree doesn't match the existing row and silently creates a new, disconnected `Workspace` — no error, just fragmented state. This was confirmed by direct inspection of the shared SQLite file, which showed two separate `Workspace` rows for what was meant to be one repository (one keyed to the main checkout's path, one to the worktree's path). The same `root_path`-keyed pattern recurs anywhere state is scoped per workspace (change tracking, content-hash dedup, the FTS/QMD index), so a naive worktree workflow trades a loud, safe failure (lock contention, retry-able) for a silent, worse one (siloed sources/memories/PR-tracking state per worktree, no error raised).

**Fix (implemented on the `worktree-git-integration` branch / PR #15, not yet merged to `main` as of 2026-07-20):** `WorkspaceConfig` now separates `root_path` (this checkout, used for file I/O) from `state_root` (where `.wakil/` lives and what a `Workspace` row is keyed on), resolved via `resolve_state_root()` in `src/wakil/config/settings.py`. For a linked worktree, `resolve_state_root()` uses `worktree_anchors()` to find the git common-dir and returns its parent (the main worktree's root); otherwise it returns `root_path` unchanged, so non-worktree usage is unaffected. All lookup sites now key on `state_root` instead of `root_path`. The branch also adds SQLite `WAL` mode plus a 30s `busy_timeout` so a writer that still loses a lock race waits instead of failing immediately, and stops `index_notes` from deleting notes just because they're absent from the current worktree's checkout.

**Why this is worth recording:** the failure mode is silent (no exception, no error path) and specific to a workflow (parallel ingest via worktrees) that this project's own agent-API plans (multiple callers hitting the same workspace concurrently) make plausible again later — worth knowing before anyone reaches for "just use worktrees" as the fix for the lock race.

### Duplicate Source rows under concurrent ingest (content-hash dedup race) — resolved

**Source:** `worktree-git-integration` branch (PR #15, still open/draft as of 2026-07-20 — not yet merged to `main`), fix commit `a14af48` ("fix(ingest): close the content-hash dedup check-then-insert race")

Under real concurrent `wakil ingest` calls, two processes ingesting identical content could both create their own `Source` row instead of one being flagged as a duplicate. Root cause: `prepare_capture`'s dedup check reads for an existing `content_hash` and `apply_capture` inserts afterward — a check-then-act (TOCTOU) race, since `content_hash` had no unique constraint at the DB level. Reproduced live (two worktrees, identical content, both got "Captured source #N" instead of the second reporting "Already ingested").

Fixed in `a14af48`:
- Migration `0004_source_content_hash_unique.py` adds `uq_sources_workspace_content_hash`, a unique index on `Source(workspace_id, content_hash)`. It first dedupes any pre-existing collisions — repointing `memories`/`relationships`/`ingest_runs` rows that reference a duplicate onto the earliest (lowest id) survivor — before adding the index, so it's safe to run against a database that already hit the race.
- `apply_capture` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`) wraps the `session.flush()` insert in a `try`/`except IntegrityError`: on the constraint violation it rolls back, deletes the raw file it had already written (avoiding an orphaned file with no `Source` row), looks up the winning `Source.id`, and raises the same "Source already ingested" error a normal duplicate-of hit would produce.

`TODO.md` on that branch marks this item `[x]` closed as of `a14af48`. This bug predated the git-worktree/state_root work and was previously masked because one of two racing `wakil ingest` processes almost always lost the `.git/index.lock` race first and exited before reaching the dedup check — concurrent ingest across worktrees is what made the race reachable in practice.

Note: as of 2026-07-20, PR #15 (which contains this fix along with the broader default-on git-landing work) has not been merged into `main`.

### `EOF while parsing a string` from a Pydantic validation error may mean the model response was truncated, not malformed

**Date:** 2026-07-20 · **Source:** `fix/entity-revision-truncation-errors` branch — `ModelTruncatedError` in `src/wakil/llm/client.py`, retry handling in `complete_with_contract` (`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`)

`wakil enrich` failed with `ModelContractError: EntityRevisionOutput: model output failed validation twice: 1 validation error for EntityRevisionOutput\n  Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a string ...`. This reads like the model produced garbage JSON, but the actual cause was `_run_entity_updates` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`) batching every `action=update` entity — 7 of them, several with long histories — into one call that asks the model to re-synthesize each note's full compiled-truth body, which exceeded the fixed `max_tokens=8192` and cut the response off mid-string. Neither `AnthropicClient` nor `OpenAICompatibleClient` (`src/wakil/llm/client.py`) checked `stop_reason`/`finish_reason` for this case, so a truncated response was indistinguishable from a genuinely malformed one until someone counted characters against the token budget.

Fixed by raising a distinct `ModelTruncatedError` when the provider reports `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` / `finish_reason == "length"`, and having `complete_with_contract`'s retry (`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`) double the token budget and resend the same prompt on truncation, instead of treating it like invalid JSON (appending the error and resending unchanged, which just truncates again at the same length). If a future model-contract call raises this same low-level symptom, check whether the call batches many items into one response before assuming the prompt or schema is wrong.
